decisions.reason: As a technically compatible drainage component with its own product-page presence in both 2018 and 2019, it still looks like a viable option to retain because carrying it likely costs less than abandoning a potentially useful platform component.
A floor-level shower drainage system matches the firm's stated direction very closely and its increased visibility by 2019 suggests enough promise to continue rather than exit.

Because this designer shower drainage line was presented as a flagship and fits the firm's design-led strategy, management would be inclined to keep investing unless there were clearly negative market signals, which are not shown here.

The integrated-slope shower element supports the firm's emphasis on installation ease and renovation solutions, so it remains worth keeping as a complementary option within the broader system offering.
Although more peripheral to the firm's bathroom-focused direction, its prominent launch and homepage visibility indicate enough market interest to justify keeping the option open for now.

The air-admittance valve appears the weakest and most peripheral of the launches, with only limited website mention and less obvious connection to the firm's core strategic push, so resources are better redeployed elsewhere.
